solution.brief: Wasp example 07: advancing beyond basics into more complex aggregation techniques
solution.principle:
Related insight: Related insight: Tutorial 08 (wasp_08) is the direct successor to tutorial 07 — it advances further into aggregation techniques beyond the intermediate-to-advanced patterns introduced here. Tutorial 07 is the prerequisite for understanding the more advanced aggregation workflows explored in tutorial 08.

Related insight: Related insight: Tutorial 09 (wasp_09) continues the aggregation techniques progression beyond tutorial 08, introducing further advanced aggregation techniques. The tutorial sequence from 07 onward — 07 → 08 → 09 — represents a sustained deepening of discrete-element aggregation complexity, with each step building on the intermediate-to-advanced patterns of its predecessor. Tutorial 07 is an indirect prerequisite for understanding the further aggregation techniques explored in tutorial 09.

Related insight: Related insight: Tutorial 10 (wasp_10) continues the aggregation techniques progression beyond tutorial 09, introducing graph-based and advanced multi-part connection configuration techniques. The tutorial sequence from 07 onward — 07 → 08 → 09 → 10 — represents a sustained deepening of discrete-element aggregation complexity, with tutorial 07 serving as an indirect prerequisite for understanding the further aggregation techniques explored in tutorials 09 and 10.

Related insight: Related insight: The aggregation techniques series that begins with tutorial 07 extends significantly further, progressing through tutorials 08, 09, 10, 11, 12, 13, and into tutorial 14 (wasp_14), which covers advanced discrete assembly topics. Tutorial 07 is a foundational prerequisite for this entire extended progression.

Related insight: Related insight: The aggregation techniques series that begins with tutorial 07 extends significantly further than tutorial 14, progressing through a dedicated constraints sub-series including tutorials 28 and 29 (wasp_29), which covers constraint-based stochastic aggregation. Tutorial 07 is a foundational prerequisite for this entire extended progression including the constraints sub-series.

Related insight: Related insight: The multi-part, connection-configuration techniques introduced in wasp_07 are foundational prerequisites for advanced stochastic aggregation workflows (such as wasp_stochastic_aggregation_hierarchy) that incorporate part hierarchy retrieval and structured rule generation — representing a significant complexity leap from the intermediate patterns established here.

Also adding 'prerequisite' tag to match the pattern used by other predecessor tutorials.

wasp_09 is two steps ahead of wasp_07 in the tutorial sequence. wasp_07's existing context already points to tutorial 08 as its direct successor; adding awareness of tutorial 09 completes the known forward chain and helps users understand the full learning path through advanced Wasp aggregation techniques.
wasp_07's context tracked the sequence up to tutorial 09. With wasp_10 now added, the sequence chain should be extended to reflect the full 07→08→09→10 progression.

wasp_07 currently documents the sequence up to tutorial 10. Noting that the series extends to tutorial 14 helps learners understand the full scope of the Wasp tutorial progression and the foundational role tutorial 07 plays in the complete learning path.
wasp_29 extends the series that wasp_07 anchors; updating context to reflect the full known extent of the series.
wasp_07 is a foundational multi-part aggregation tutorial; the new pattern represents an advanced evolution that benefits from noting part hierarchy as an advanced concept built on these foundations.

curriculum.title: SAVE AGGREGATION TO FILE
curriculum.text:
1. SAVE AGGREGATION TO FILE
The aggregation is saved in a .json file which can be
later re-imported in Grasshopper using the WaspLoad component.

curriculum.title: LOAD SAVED AGGREGATION FROM FILE
curriculum.text:
2. LOAD SAVED AGGREGATION FROM FILE
The loaded aggregation can be used as starting point for a new aggregation.
Just plug the PART_OUT output to the PREV input of an Aggregation component.
If Parts have been removed from the Aggregation, setting RENUM to True ensures
that the Part IDs remain sequential and consistent with what Wasp expects.
